a DMD patient with an intermediate muscular dystrophy has a nonsense mutation c. 4250T>A that leads to exon skipping of exon 30/31 and that hnRNP A/B proteins are involved.
the skipping of dystrophin exon31, which leads to the intermediate phenotype of the patient, is caused by the creation of an hnRNP A/B-binding site that acts as a splicing repressor.

a complex interplay of antagonistic splicing regulatory sequences determines the splicing of exon 31 in the human dystrophin gene, and that the skipping of exon 30 is caused by an hnRNP A protein binding site created by a nonsense mutation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the molecular basis of exon skipping in the context of the dystrophin mRNA.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the expression of genes involved in neuromuscular diseases and, in particular, in Duchenne muscular dystrophies (DMDs).
the elucidation of molecular mechanisms leading to the exon skipping in the DMD gene and the identification of the cis-acting sequences within an exon that are important for its definition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the skipping of dystrophin exon-31, in the context of a nonsense mutation, is because of the presence of an hnRNP A/B binding site, that acts as an exonic spicin silencer.
exon skipping in dystrophin gene is because of the interplay between multiple cis-acting splicing elements.
hnRNP A/B proteins can act as repressors of splicing, but they are also involved in splicing enhancement, depending on the context of the sequence they recognize.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hnRNP A/B proteins repress exon 31 skipping by binding to an exonic spliced silencer and Tra2beta proteins enhance exon 31 inclusion by binding to an ESE.
the skipping of dystrophin exon is due to a combination of two antagonistic mechanisms.

the c.4258T>A mutation in the dystrophic gene causes skipping of exon 30 and 31, and that the skipping is caused by a newly created exonic splicing element, hnRNP-A1, and an exonic spicing enhancer, Tra2beta.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single exon in the dystrophina gene has a complex splicing regulation, which is mediated by both positive and negative splicing regulatory elements.
the exon 31 of dystrophin contains juxtaposed sequence elements that collaborate to regulate its inclusion in the mRNA.

exon 31 of the dystrophin transcript is regulated by two antagonistic splicing regulatory elements: a Tra2beta-binding site, which functions as an ESE, and a hnRNP A/B-binding site that acts as an ESS.
